name: redb (copy-on-write B+tree KV store)
baseline: RocksDB (rust-rocksdb 0.22) and SQLite (rusqlite 0.37, bundled, default rollback journal) as key-value stores
verdict_reason: redb is 2.6x faster than RocksDB on random reads and durable single-row commits, and beats SQLite on reads and small writes. It loses to RocksDB on batch writes (3.5x slower), removals (3.4x) and bulk load (1.2x), loses to SQLite on bulk load and removals, its files are 4.6x larger than RocksDB's, and LMDB beats it on every read test.
tier_reason: Benchmark source is in the repository, the toolchain is pinned by rust-toolchain (1.89), and CPU and SSD are stated.
claimed_speedup: vs RocksDB: random reads 1138 vs 2911 ms (2.6x faster), individual writes 920 vs 2432 ms (2.6x faster); vs SQLite: random reads 1138 vs 4283 ms (3.8x), individual writes 920 vs 7040 ms (7.7x). Slower than RocksDB on batch writes (1595 vs 451 ms), removals (23297 vs 6900 ms) and bulk load (17063 vs 13969 ms); uncompacted size 4.00 GiB vs 893.18 MiB (ratios derived from page data).
workload: 5 million random 24-byte keys with 150-byte values: bulk load, 1,000 durable single-insert transactions, 100 batches of 1,000, 1 million random reads and range reads (1 to 32 threads), removals; 4 GB cache.
toolchain: rustc 1.89 (rust-toolchain file at the benchmark commit), cargo bench release profile
platforms: Any Rust target with a file system; no_std with a custom storage backend
one_liner: Pure-Rust ACID key-value store; 2.6x faster reads and single commits than RocksDB, but slower batch writes and larger files.
how_it_is_fast: Data lives in copy-on-write B+trees with MVCC, so readers never block and a point read is a short tree walk with no compaction or bloom-filter work. A durable commit writes the changed pages and flips a root pointer. The cost is write amplification on bulk and batch writes and no compression on disk.
use_it_when: Read-heavy embedded storage with many small durable transactions
You want a pure-Rust store with a typed BTreeMap-like API instead of RocksDB's C++ build
skip_it_when: Write-heavy ingestion in large batches, or delete-heavy workloads: RocksDB and fjall are faster
Disk space matters: files were 4.6x larger than RocksDB's before compaction
Pure read latency is all that matters: LMDB (heed) was faster on every read test
caveats: First-party benchmark written by redb's author
README numbers were collected in August 2025 with redb 2.6.0; redb is now 4.4.0 and the benchmark code has changed since
SQLite ran with defaults (rollback journal, no WAL, synchronous FULL on durable writes), which understates it
tradeoffs: No on-disk compression; space use is the highest of the engines tested
Single writer at a time per database (multi-writer mode is newly stabilized)

evidence.quote: redb has similar performance to other top embedded key-value stores such as lmdb and rocksdb
| uncompacted size | 4.00 GiB | 2.61 GiB | **893.18 MiB** | 1000.95 MiB | 1.09 GiB |
Results collected on a Ryzen 9950X3D with Samsung 9100 PRO NVMe.
